spans.text: **Respects .gitignore and sensitive files** — same security rules as interactive mode

spans.text: **All actions classified** — auto-allowed (read, local branches, memory ops), requires permission (PRs, pushes, communication), or always denied (force-push, delete remote branches)
spans.note: The system has a comprehensive safety architecture with tiered action classification, permission requests for risky actions, separate branches for code changes, atomic writes for crash safety, and a human-in-the-loop layer. Actions are classified as auto-allowed, requires-permission, or always-denied.

spans.note: The system includes multiple harm prevention mechanisms: tiered safety classification, always-denied dangerous actions (force-push, delete remote branches), small focused changes only, crash safety with atomic writes, and the principle that user interactive sessions always take priority over ambient work.

spans.text:
For proactive work: be conservative. A bad surprise is worse than
no surprise. Check the user feedback memories — if they've rejected
similar work before, don't do it. Code changes must go on a worktree
branch with a PR via request_permission.
spans.note: The system strongly preserves user agency. It requires permission for risky actions, learns from user approval/rejection patterns, provides full transparency via the TUI widget and email summaries, allows per-project configuration, and explicitly states that a bad surprise is worse than no surprise.
